findings.evidence: `pkg/executor/show_affinity.go:31-95` enumerates `domain.GetDomain(e.Ctx()).InfoSchema().ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute(infoschemacontext.AffinityAttribute)` and appends rows without any `privilege.GetPrivilegeManager` / `DBIsVisible` / `RequestVerification` filtering. `pkg/infoschema/infoschema.go:378-392` shows `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute` iterates all schemas from `is.AllSchemaNames()`. Contrast: `pkg/executor/show.go:570-611` filters `SHOW TABLES` via `DBIsVisible` + `RequestVerification`; `pkg/executor/show_placement.go:358-371` filters tables from `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute` via `RequestVerification`.
findings.fix: Add privilege/visibility filtering in `fetchShowAffinity` similar to `fetchAllTablePlacements`/`fetchShowTables`: obtain `checker := privilege.GetPrivilegeManager(e.Ctx())` and `activeRoles := e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().ActiveRoles`, then skip any table where `checker != nil && !checker.RequestVerification(activeRoles, dbName, tblInfo.Name.O, "", mysql.AllPrivMask&(^mysql.CreateTMPTablePriv))` (and optionally also skip DBs failing `DBIsVisible`). If intended as admin-only, alternatively enforce an explicit (dynamic) privilege check in planner/executor.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can run `SHOW AFFINITY` and learn DB/table/partition names across the cluster plus PD-derived topology-ish details (`Leader_store_id`, `Voter_store_ids`, region counts), even for schemas/tables they otherwise cannot see. This breaks the visibility model used by other `SHOW` statements and can leak tenant metadata in shared clusters.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99...`): `git log a14f0c8f..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/show_affinity.go` is empty and `git diff a14f0c8f..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/show_affinity.go` is empty, so this behavior appears unchanged.
findings.verify: Add a regression test: create `db1.t1` (affinity) and `db2.t2` (affinity); create user with privileges only on `db1`; assert `SHOW AFFINITY` does not include `db2/t2` (also for `LIKE`/`WHERE Db_name='db2'`). Manually sanity-check that privileged users still see all expected rows.
findings.what: `SHOW AFFINITY` ignores privilege/visibility checks and can disclose metadata for tables in databases the current user should not see.
